A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CaRe-BN work, with matching core equations, pseudocode and main comparison table. Their text and visual material support comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes substantial appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo experiments, including learning curves, exploration results, component ablations and comparisons in Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional Atari, SAC, distribution-error, simulation-step and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same adaptive updates and recalibration procedure. However, v1 Equation 10 uses previous moving estimates for prediction, whereas v2 Section 4.2 footnote 2 specifies previous minibatch statistics, conflicting with its unchanged pseudocode. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an intended procedural change or a notation error.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from MuJoCo continuous control to RAM-based Atari discrete control. Figure 7 reports Pong, Breakout, Freeway, Seaquest and SpaceInvaders. The original five MuJoCo environments remain.

E2.justification: The main CLIF/TD3 comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged. However, v2 Table 16 adds tdBN, BNTT, TEBN and TABN to the LIF/TD3 comparison, where v1 Figure 4 compared CaRe-BN with vanilla LIF. This extends comparator participation within an existing experimental configuration.

E3.justification: v2 adds DQN and SAC experimental setups, Dynamic Neuron configurations, simulation lengths of 2, 3 and 8 steps, a Wasserstein-distance evaluation, and timing, memory and energy-estimation protocols. The retained main experiments still use five simulation steps and ten evaluation trials. Newly supplied settings for existing experiments are documentation rather than established protocol revisions.

E4.justification: New analyses directly quantify layerwise BN distribution mismatch (Figure 3), test sensitivity to simulation length (Table 17), and assess training overhead and estimated inference energy (Tables 20–21). The original Ca-BN/Re-BN component ablation is retained as Figure 6(c). These additions substantially broaden mechanistic, sensitivity and efficiency analysis.

E5.justification: v1 states that each algorithm uses five random seeds. v2 retains five-seed reporting for MuJoCo but specifies three seeds for the added Atari experiments in Figure 7. Half-standard-deviation shading and mean-plus-or-minus-standard-deviation tables remain the reporting conventions; no increased run count is established for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1 scores, including the 5.90% APG, and the original component-ablation values are unchanged. v2 adds Atari, SAC and Dynamic Neuron results, distribution-error measurements, detailed appendix results and cost estimates. Table 17 newly reports APGs of -23.80% at two simulation steps and 6.32% at eight steps; these are additional settings, not improvements to the unchanged five-step result.

T1.justification: The central optimal-weight theorem, proof and Gaussian assumption remain. Section 4.2 adds a mathematical assertion that squared minibatch deviations provide unbiased variance probes, while Appendix D.1.2 adds encoder-gradient derivations with an explicit surrogate-derivative assumption. These are limited additions to the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the explicitly demonstrated scope from continuous control to both discrete and continuous control. The principal two-component contribution, SNN-specific normalization positioning, unchanged inference claim, and headline 22.6% and 5.9% performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4.6 adds discussion of performance dependence on simulation length and explains retaining five steps for consistency with prior studies despite stronger eight-step results. Section 4.2 expands the rationale for estimating confidence from minibatch deviations. The main exploration-feedback explanation and interpretation of limited ANN benefits remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies architecture and surrogate-gradient details, neuron parameters, preprocessing, hardware and extensive RL hyperparameter tables absent from the supplied v1. Table 4 specifies momentum 0.8, recalibration every 5000 steps and 100 calibration batches. It also adds code-access information. These substantially improve documentation without establishing that retained experiments changed implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Atari evaluation, RL normalization context and energy estimation, and discusses Xu et al. (2026) on continuous-control ANN-to-SNN conversion. It also explicitly acknowledges the already-cited Proxy Target framework's ability to surpass ANNs. The central positioning around SNN-RL normalization remains.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. Local revisions expand the motivation, confidence-estimation explanation and experimental setup, while new appendix organization, acknowledgments, disclosure statements and conference/contact text improve navigation and documentation. The main narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, expands the learning-curve figure with Dynamic Neuron rows, and adds distribution-error, Atari, SAC and detailed ANN plots. Numerous settings, results and cost tables create a substantial new appendix presentation. Existing exploration and component-ablation figures are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reproducibility by supplying the implementation details and hyperparameters that v1 referred to but did not include. Direct distribution-error measurements, Atari/SAC evaluation, simulation-length sensitivity and cost analyses materially strengthen empirical support beyond the unchanged headline scores. The conflicting prediction footnote and some labeling errors limit precision, but do not outweigh these substantial gains in documentation and validation.
